questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me it was absolutely crucial to visit a place with beautiful nature, endless travel opportunities as well as good academic facilities (easy transportation, international courses, high level).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A bit difficult due to the difficult portals and ways of finding information online. You have to be really patient and look several places upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Very very difficult systems to navigate in. I was terribly confused a lot of times, and it was extremely difficult to find relevant information, destinations, course-selection and academic transcripts. 4-5 different portals you need to use before- and during your stay.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Difficult. My best advise is to visit AirBnB and try to work out long term rental deals as well as
flatmates.au
. Me and all my friends found housing through AirBnB

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Public transportation is not very interconnected, and often you need to use serveral ways of transportation to reach USNW as it is a bit far away from city centre.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in Paddington which was an amazing location (in the posh area of Sydney). 20 min from Bondi and 20 min. from CBD. I would recommend living in Surry Hills or Darlinghurst as well. Also Newtown is more reasonable to pay and has a really nice vibe - however even more far out and further away from the beach!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really difficult and outdated systems to apply through and no security in the course selection.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Completely online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mail, but with extremely long answer times. Not too professional tbh.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Semi. Got two of 4 i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient and expect to have to do research in advance. also keep track of all the different portals and pages.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really easy compared to danish education. Mostly written assignments. demands were not very high in regards to getting honours and distinction. Remember to be active in class - that will give you great scores.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was generally low. It is very easy to adapt to the english language. They do not work case-based bot purely theoretical, which makes it even easier to adapt to their law system.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: No case, very many class-debates, many presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Responses to corporate wrongdoing
Indigenous Peoples in international law
Introduction to the Australian legal system in a comparative perspective
Sport, Law and Society in Australia

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them. Very easy. All assignment based, so no final exams. I got of already in late april and had plenty of time to travel around!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So fun to stay in Sydney. So many activities and societies to join: night life, beach clibs, surfing, running, arts etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Tennis, trekking, danish societies.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sports activities for sure! Engaging with other exchange students and find travel partners.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: West Australia - best experience ever. As well as Melbourne and New Zealand. Also, do the hike to figure-8 pools

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. People are very friendly and enganging. However don't necessarily expect to find many australian friends. it is more the other excange students you befriend as the australian natives are already settled.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The love of nature, friendly people, multicultural city, chill vibes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Save Up and use all your money on travelling
Use all of your spare time on exploring nature in- and around Sydney
Engange in exchange student communities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of social offers - remember it is okay to sit back and relax and not jump on every opportunity.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My travelling - completely life changing. My memories lift me up everyday, and not a day pass by where i don't think of Sydney.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being so far from home. Prepare to feel disconnected.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
